why: The history reply's outcome stops being stale{as_of} and becomes a plain fetched -- the shape a degrade that overwrites the resource's freshness produces. Two things answer, and BOTH are the point. A7: expect.statuses names outcome stale{as_of} AND degraded{local_id,bytes} on the same entry, and no entry carries the stale one any more. A2: the host derives staleness per resource from that resource's own outcome, so all three surviving observations are now stamped `live` where expect.ledger declares `cached`. That second half exists only because staleness is compared in ledger entries; strip it back out and this mutant produces {A7} alone and the battery goes red, which is the whole reason it is written down as a pair. Staleness cannot be flipped for ONE observation of the three: it is a per-resource derivation from one status, so the smallest real break is this one.
